notes.title: Screen Explosion @ Electro-Magnetic Field - also, could you write a review?
notes.notes:
[h3]Screen Explosion Live![/h3]

The [b]Jean-Paul Software Screen Explosion![/b] will be on display at the fabulous [url=https://emfcamp.org]Electromagnetic Field Festival[/url] this summer! 

Running from the 30th of May to the 2nd of June, EMF is probably the most unique festival going, featuring everything from games to music to talks that show [i]TED[/i] to be the bland agglomeration of self-promoting midwits it really is.

[previewyoutube=UWQuMnWcmwc;full][/previewyoutube]

Tickets are sold out, but keep checking the website and you may get lucky. They're also open to submissions for exhibits and talks, so if you've got something to show, or a talk about how to hack your toaster so can embed QR codes into your breakfast, then get in touch with the organisers.

If you're already coming down sure to say hi- you'll be able to tell who I am, because I have a beard and glasses, which is a very unique combination, particularly amongst people who work with computers.

[h3]And also...[/h3]

if you're enjoying the Screen Explosion, could you write a review? The Steam Recommendation Algorithm is a cruel thing, and looks more kindly on things with more reviews.

Cheers, and hopefully see at least some of you in Hereford.

-Ed / JPS

notes.title: Custom colour palettes now available
notes.notes:
The four screensavers with user-selectable colour palettes now have the option to create your own! Now you can finally create your country's flag with fish.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/4abf18c39eabdaebe407a22d519f6e7e484da6ea.png[/img]

You can add as many palettes as you want, and select whether they're enabled or disabled for if you have the 'random' palette on. You can also disable the native palettes if you want. 

Some tips-

[list]
[*] There's a maximum and minimum number of colours for each screensaver. When you create a palette, it will be set with the minimum. The maximum for most is 20, except The Sublimnotron, where there have to be three colours- no more, no less
[*] The first colour is usually the background the colour. The exception for this is The Haunted Carpet, which (for now) always has a black background
[*] Colours for fish will probably have to be relatively light, since that one has lighting applied, and the colours will spend at least some time in shadow. If the colours are too dark, they'll just show up as black, so boost the lightness a bit.
[/list]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/2fe9e00ee2aa7ad6731d85a9205590b25415414f.png[/img]

Enjoy, and as ever, let me know if anything goes wrong, or you have any suggestions

Cheers,

-Ed / Jean-Paul Software

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/9906f882612aa8aaf88b55fe9b9ec6ed9e620725.jpg[/img]

notes.title: This new 3D screensaver collection includes a driving tour of global pylons
notes.notes:
The first time a PC seemed magical to me was when it dozed off and colourful lines twisted across its screen. I'd launch Windows 3.1 just to watch screensavers, marvelling at Mystify and staring at Starfield. How wonderful that our computer needed to dream as preventative medicine! I relived this today with a new collection of customisable 3D screensavers, watching shoals of fish, taking a road trip through a museum of global electricity pylons, watching housing estates rise and fall, and seeing so many swirly colours.

notes.notes:
New screensaver- The Haunted Carpet. 

I had a request to do something like the 'drift' screensaver that's in MacOS. Not wanting to do an exact clone I had a bit of a play, and after some fiddling with a compute shader I wound up with The Haunted Carpet.  

I could have given it a "cool" name like 'drift' or 'flow' or whatever, but It looks like a haunted carpet, so that's what it's called. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/ca3ef20e8682b1a68e261017dd6d16749ce585d0.jpg[/img]

There's three density settings (or should that be shag settings?), and five colours schemes to choose from, including Baize Moi, Pile Driver, and Straight Outta Brompton. If you have any other carpet-related puns, please add them in the comments and I'll add a new colour scheme for each.

Enjoy!

notes.title: New Screensaver: North Pole Logistics

New this Christmas to the Jean-Paul Software Screen Explosion: The North Pole Logistics Centre! Due to population increase and concerns about delivering presents in person during a world-wide pandemic, Santa has embraced mechanisation, recycled the majority of his elves, and moved over to present sorting by drone.

notes.title: New Screensaver: DEADLINE
notes.notes:
It's Hallowe'en, a time of creepy things, but nothing actually scary. Plastic spiders are not scary, and neither are pubs that put fake spider webs in the window. Sexy nurse can be scary, but frequently isn't; the whole cat ears thing I don't understand but I am not one to fear the incomprehensible.

But you know what is scary? Death. Specifically, [b]your[/b] death.

So! The Jean-Paul Software Screen Explosion now has a new screensaver, entitled [b]DEADLINE[/b], designed to show the passing of time and the miserable grind of life. Set it active, and you will gain an uncomfortable awareness of just how long you have left in the only world you have ever known*. Or maybe a comforting awareness- as Earl Brutus once said, life's too long.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/8576c225087574ed51378eaff033f3c4e8c9d0e3.png[/img]

Enter your birthdate, country of birth, and sex (if you choose), and the software will estimate the date of your death. Then, get a live countdown to that day, in hours, every time you view your screensaver. Or, use it to keep track of when a celebrity you hate is going to die! Or your boss, or husband, or whoever- as long as you buy the software I don't really care what you do with it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/06fb4e51e4b6a73906c89abf976bac4e3b82147c.png[/img]

Happy Hallowe'en!

- Ed / Jean-Paul Software

P.S. according to the statistics I plugged into this Rupert Murdoch should be dead right now. 

* [i]If you have solid evidence of knowing other worlds, please present it on, like, Reddit?[/i]

notes.title: Stability improvements
notes.notes:
Windows has some interesting rules about handling screensavers- namely, if they're not in [i]Windows/System32[/i] then they become somewhat flaky. Changing your power settings can cause them to vanish from the list of screensavers completely, as can temporarily turning them off; and sometimes restarting your computer can do it, and some other things I've yet to properly identify.

This update does two key things:
[list]
[*] Separates the 'screensaver' bit of the code from the 'fancy graphics' bit of the code
[*] Adds an option when setting the screensaver to copy the screensaver part to [i]Windows/System32[/i] folder
[/list]

The separation of 'fancy graphics' from 'screensaver' means we can have a small .scr file that connects to the bigger application when it needs to. Whilst I was at it I finally bit the bullet, dived into the Windows API, and implemented a preview image when viewing the screensaver:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41170677/a1d9ebe947eb2563c4133285a1173ba8d6819ed5.png[/img]

Copying to the system folder is entirely optional, but at some point in early access I hope to get a proper install / uninstall script working that handles adding and removing this automatically. You shouldn't need to go through the process again if everything has been running properly for you; Windows will just use the updated .scr file.

Next up: more features!

notes.title: Steam integration now even more optional
notes.notes: After playing around with Steam's DRM solution I found that restarting the screensaver through Steam was causing the user power settings to be ignored. Windows would assume the screensaver had terminated and the 'screen off' setting would never trigger. As far as I'm concerned that's too big a price to pay for DRM- you're buying a screensaver, not an invitation for an unintended power bill- so DRM is gone.

notes.title: Preparing for release and what comes after
notes.notes:
So, hopefully, on the 28th of September, this will be ready for release! Big thanks to everyone who has helped test things so far. If you've got the time, I'd really appreciate it if people could continue to give it a good shakedown. If there's anything that jumps out, please let me know, but as far as I'm aware nearly all the bugs are dealt with. I will continue to post patch notes here, however.

After release, what's next? 

Well, the next big addition is going to be a Hallowe'en screensaver, because people love Hallowe'en. The prototype I've got is *quite* disturbing, but I'm hoping to ramp that up to *very* disturbing.

Workshop support will be added to more of the modules, in particular Probably Enough Fish and Pylons of the World. I am looking forward to seeing flocks of memes floating around.

I'll also be dealing with bug reports, which hopefully won't take up too much time. I've not done a great deal of testing on non-NVidia graphics hardware; there is the possibility this will bite me in the arse.

I owe all of you a beer, and hopefully will be able to give it to you in person

Cheers,

-Ed

notes.title: Steam integration now optional
notes.notes:
As requested, there's now an option in the settings that disables the Steam integration when the screensaver is launched. To access this, go to [b]settings -> set as screensaver[/b] and uncheck the box marked 'Steam integration enabled'.

If disabled, it won't restart Steam if it's not running when the app is launched as a screensaver. You won't however be able to use items in the workshop, or get the achievements, but on the other hand it should be less likely to show you the latest Midweek Madness deal when it exits.

Also, I can upload announcements now we're visible on Steam, how good is that?
